Details of the IPO, including the demand for shares, could change, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity. Anthropic declined to comment.
During the roadshow, investors are grappling with two fundamental questions as they assess the offering and the company's valuation: whether Anthropic can maintain its lead as competitors such as Alphabet’s Google rapidly catch up in developing advanced AI models, and whether its Claude chatbot can maintain its lead beyond coding, in the broader market for knowledge workers.
TIME OF UNCERTAINTY IN AI
The questions underscore the challenge of valuing a company whose revenue is growing fast but whose long-term competitive position remains uncertain. Investors are trying to determine whether the AI industry will ultimately be dominated by one or two players or support several leading companies, and whether Anthropic can sustain premium pricing if rivals offer comparable models.
Meanwhile, investors are also weighing the limitations of the information Anthropic is providing during its IPO roadshow. One investor who attended a roadshow meeting said the company had not provided detailed answers to some of the questions raised. Anthropic declined to comment on the investor's remarks.
While companies are not always able to address every investor question during roadshows, some investors remain cautious about an offering at a high valuation amid a broader shakeout in the AI sector, with the limited disclosure leaving some questions unanswered.
One of the group meetings during the roadshow also did not include a conference call allowing institutional investors to dial in and ask questions, according to an investor who attended that meeting — a departure from standard roadshow practice. Representatives from Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley largely read from prepared remarks rather than solicit  questions at that meeting, the person added.
Morgan Stanley declined to comment. Goldman Sachs did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
REVENUE AT CENTER OF VALUATION DEBATE
Investors are arriving at widely different estimates of how quickly Anthropic's revenue will grow, creating a broad range of potential valuation outcomes.
The key figure underpinning valuation models is Anthropic's projected 2028 revenue, which banks estimate at around $270 billion to $280 billion and use to apply enterprise-value-to-revenue multiples and arrive at their valuation estimates, two of the people familiar with the projections said. For a high-growth company like Anthropic, investors typically give significant weight to future revenue growth when assessing its value.
Some sell-side projections put Anthropic's revenue at around $52 billion to $53 billion in 2026, rising to $135 billion to $137 billion in  2027, one of the people said.
Certain buy-side projections are running 10 per cent to 15 per cent higher for 2026 and 2027, an investor who has placed an order in the IPO said.
But buy-side forecasts also vary significantly. One investor who conducted due diligence on the IPO but decided not to participate has a more conservative outlook that is about 30 per cent below the sell-side estimate for 2028.
Differences between sell-side and buy-side forecasts are common. Sell-side analysts' estimates tend to track a company's own projections more closely, while investors may build in more optimistic or conservative assumptions about future growth. Companies, in turn, have an incentive to set conservative targets ahead of an IPO, leaving room to beat estimates and raise expectations after listing.
The comparable companies used in the valuation models also reflect the difficulty of finding direct peers for Anthropic. SpaceX and cybersecurity company CrowdStrike are among the names being used as benchmarks, one of the people familiar with the projections said.
The focus on Anthropic's projected 2028 revenue contrasts with SpaceX, whose valuation case relied on projected 2029 revenue that some investors viewed as particularly aggressive. Anthropic's valuation debate, by comparison, is anchored in a forecast for a year closer to its expected public listing. 

Source: Reuters

[ワシントン １３日 ロイター] - 米連邦航空局（ＦＡＡ）は１３日、全米の空港に対し全ての航空機の離陸停止措置を命じた。航空管制センターで通信障害が発生したことが理由。

フライト追跡サービス「FlightAware」によると、この措置により約７０００便が遅延または欠航となった。

飛行中の航空機は着陸できるが、地上にある航空機は離陸できない。

全米規模で出発便が地上待機となる措置が取られるのは、２００１年９月１１日の米同時多発攻撃以降で２回目。前回は２０２３年１月で、国内線の出発便が２時間近く停止された。

The trilateral discussion is expected to focus largely on developing an ambitious nuclear arms control pact, but discussions could also touch on North Korea and the Iran war, the Post reported.

Trump has already publicly indicated that he planned to meet with the two leaders.

items.title: Commentary: Jensen Huang may prove that the ‘irreplaceable CEO’ is a myth
items.author: Beth Kowitt
items.summary: Jensen Huang's successor will have to figure out how to run a company built around someone who is no longer there, says Beth Kowitt for Bloomberg Opinion.

Commentary: Jensen Huang may prove that the ‘irreplaceable CEO’ is a myth

Jensen Huang's successor will have to figure out how to run a company built around someone who is no longer there, says Beth Kowitt for Bloomberg Opinion.

Jensen Huang, president and CEO of Nvidia, waits for a groundbreaking ceremony for an expansion of Coherent's manufacturing facility to begin on Jun 16, 2026, in Sherman, Texas. (Photo: AP/Jeffrey McWhorter)

Beth Kowitt

Beth Kowitt

NEW YORK: “He’s irreplaceable,” Larry Ellison said.
The year was 2009 and Oracle’s then-chief executive officer was talking about his friend Steve Jobs, who had recently returned to lead Apple after a liver transplant. Pundits would later go on to say the same about Jeff Bezos, that Amazon.com’s founder and CEO had “no viable successor”. (Both companies, of course, would go on to do just fine without their founders.)
It’s worth remembering those prophecies as that word - irreplaceable - gets bandied around with abandon about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down Thursday (Nov 12) after nearly a week of turmoil at the company he cofounded and the industry he anchored. 
One of many examples: “I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership,” Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire posted on X, a sentiment Elon Musk endorsed.

Revelations from the New York Times on Wednesday, that Huang had an extramarital relationship with the company’s vice president of healthcare, made it impossible for the board to let him keep his job. While less shocking than Huang’s earlier admission that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, he had clearly violated the company’s code of conduct to “avoid situations where our actions create a conflict”.
Before board members could make the case that Huang was the victim of a honeypot scheme. But there’s no convenient explanation for a relationship with a subordinate.

CAN NVIDIA SURVIVE WITHOUT JENSEN HUANG? The board named CFO Collette Kress as the interim CEO, but now its members will have to plan for a future without Huang at the helm. This appears to be something they had rarely considered before, after allowing Huang to structure the company almost entirely around himself. The question now is whether he had also built it to survive without him. As Harvard Business School professor Rakesh Khurana put it to me: “The difference between a cult and a religion is that one outlasts the other.”
At Nvidia, the evidence suggests that Huang created a system much more akin to the former. 
The company has no chairman, no number two and no public succession plan. Huang had 60 direct reports whose job it was to quickly carry out his decisions, Bloomberg News has reported. Few other executives had a broad purview or responsibilities and instead focused on narrow products or technologies. Other executives had some public exposure but were always overshadowed by Huang, who delivered hours-long keynotes at events. 
On earnings calls, as the Wall Street Journal noted, Huang fielded questions from analysts mostly by himself, leaving scripted comments to others - a regular practice at Nvidia but atypical at other companies. His board lacked the expected heavy hitters for a company of its size and import; other than Huang, it has no sitting CEOs.

Related:

Commentary: Everything Jensen Huang said about China is out the window

Commentary: Jensen Huang is bigger than Nvidia – and it’s a problem

A REAL FAILURE OF LEADERSHIP? None of that necessarily means Huang can’t be replaced. There was no finding another Jobs or Bezos either - they were both singular leaders. But what they did, which appears to be missing at Nvidia, was methodically build companies designed to carry on their doctrines without them.
Both created internal structures that institutionalised their ways of operating and thinking that allowed their successors to thrive: Apple’s stock returned nearly 2,800 per cent during Tim Cook’s 15-year tenure as CEO that ended in September; Andy Jassy has overseen a roughly 50 per cent increase since he took over at Amazon in 2021.
At Apple, Jobs was a micromanager who was involved in every detail of the company. But he also taught employees to anticipate how he would solve problems. “The organization has been thoroughly trained to think like Steve,” Fortune reported in 2009. “People could envision, ‘This is what Steve would do.'” 
He also had a clear number two in Cook, a manufacturing and supply chain guru, who had a trial run as CEO when Jobs was out on medical leave. Jobs made sure it wasn’t always the Steve Jobs show either. Cook and other executives were given public exposure by appearing alongside him on stage and on earnings calls. (It’s worth noting that Cook is being floated as a possible replacement for Huang, including by President Trump.)
At Amazon, Bezos turned his management philosophy into an actionable way of operating - a set of leadership principles that Jassy and other executives helped him write. Bezos picked Jassy as his first shadow, a role in which he followed around the CEO for about 18 months. That’s when the two came up with the idea for Amazon Web Services, and then Bezos gave Jassy a wide berth to run it. By the time Jassy was tapped as CEO, he had already run a hugely important and valuable business.
Part of the genius of both Bezos and Jobs was that they figured out how to turn their personal capabilities into corporate culture and competencies. 
The parallels are hard to find at Nvidia, which is a real failure of leadership by Huang. His successor will have to figure out how to run a company built around someone who is no longer there. That should be one part of Huang’s legacy that no one tries to replicate.

Source: Bloomberg/sk

It’s worth remembering those prophecies as that word - irreplaceable - gets bandied around with abandon about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down Thursday (Nov 12) after nearly a week of turmoil at the company he cofounded and the industry he anchored. 
One of many examples: “I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership,” Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire posted on X, a sentiment Elon Musk endorsed.

Revelations from the New York Times on Wednesday, that Huang had an extramarital relationship with the company’s vice president of healthcare, made it impossible for the board to let him keep his job. While less shocking than Huang’s earlier admission that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, he had clearly violated the company’s code of conduct to “avoid situations where our actions create a conflict”.
Before board members could make the case that Huang was the victim of a honeypot scheme. But there’s no convenient explanation for a relationship with a subordinate.

CAN NVIDIA SURVIVE WITHOUT JENSEN HUANG? The board named CFO Collette Kress as the interim CEO, but now its members will have to plan for a future without Huang at the helm. This appears to be something they had rarely considered before, after allowing Huang to structure the company almost entirely around himself. The question now is whether he had also built it to survive without him. As Harvard Business School professor Rakesh Khurana put it to me: “The difference between a cult and a religion is that one outlasts the other.”
At Nvidia, the evidence suggests that Huang created a system much more akin to the former. 
The company has no chairman, no number two and no public succession plan. Huang had 60 direct reports whose job it was to quickly carry out his decisions, Bloomberg News has reported. Few other executives had a broad purview or responsibilities and instead focused on narrow products or technologies. Other executives had some public exposure but were always overshadowed by Huang, who delivered hours-long keynotes at events. 
On earnings calls, as the Wall Street Journal noted, Huang fielded questions from analysts mostly by himself, leaving scripted comments to others - a regular practice at Nvidia but atypical at other companies. His board lacked the expected heavy hitters for a company of its size and import; other than Huang, it has no sitting CEOs.

Related:

Commentary: Everything Jensen Huang said about China is out the window

Commentary: Jensen Huang is bigger than Nvidia – and it’s a problem

A REAL FAILURE OF LEADERSHIP? None of that necessarily means Huang can’t be replaced. There was no finding another Jobs or Bezos either - they were both singular leaders. But what they did, which appears to be missing at Nvidia, was methodically build companies designed to carry on their doctrines without them.
Both created internal structures that institutionalised their ways of operating and thinking that allowed their successors to thrive: Apple’s stock returned nearly 2,800 per cent during Tim Cook’s 15-year tenure as CEO that ended in September; Andy Jassy has overseen a roughly 50 per cent increase since he took over at Amazon in 2021.
At Apple, Jobs was a micromanager who was involved in every detail of the company. But he also taught employees to anticipate how he would solve problems. “The organization has been thoroughly trained to think like Steve,” Fortune reported in 2009. “People could envision, ‘This is what Steve would do.'” 
He also had a clear number two in Cook, a manufacturing and supply chain guru, who had a trial run as CEO when Jobs was out on medical leave. Jobs made sure it wasn’t always the Steve Jobs show either. Cook and other executives were given public exposure by appearing alongside him on stage and on earnings calls. (It’s worth noting that Cook is being floated as a possible replacement for Huang, including by President Trump.)
At Amazon, Bezos turned his management philosophy into an actionable way of operating - a set of leadership principles that Jassy and other executives helped him write. Bezos picked Jassy as his first shadow, a role in which he followed around the CEO for about 18 months. That’s when the two came up with the idea for Amazon Web Services, and then Bezos gave Jassy a wide berth to run it. By the time Jassy was tapped as CEO, he had already run a hugely important and valuable business.
Part of the genius of both Bezos and Jobs was that they figured out how to turn their personal capabilities into corporate culture and competencies. 
The parallels are hard to find at Nvidia, which is a real failure of leadership by Huang. His successor will have to figure out how to run a company built around someone who is no longer there. That should be one part of Huang’s legacy that no one tries to replicate.

The incident follows recent security concerns, with US military aircraft moved from British bases reportedly due to threats from Iran.

LONDON: United States Air Force personnel at the RAF Lakenheath base in Britain responded to "suspected unauthorised drone activity" on Friday (Nov 13) evening, although no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, a US Air Force spokesperson said.
"We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families," the spokesperson added.
Britain's Ministry of Defence said US Air Force Security Forces personnel had responded to reports of unauthorised drone activity and that the situation had been resolved.
"We are working closely with them to establish the facts. We will provide updates in due course," a ministry spokesperson said in an emailed statement.

T he US has in recent weeks moved bombers that had been used to strike Iran out of Britain, and relocated huge refuelling aircraft from Britain to Germany. The Wall Street Journal has reported that the refuelling aircraft were moved due to a threat from Iran.
The bombers left RAF Fairford on security grounds after a group of men approached the base in white vans in the middle of the night on Sep 27.
Two men were charged last month in relation to that incident, with prosecutors alleging one of them had tried to assist Iranian intelligence in Britain.
The US Justice Department said this week that a member of an Iran-backed militia had plotted to attack the Fairford air base while detained in the US on criminal charges.
Britain's domestic spy chief said in October that Iran had stepped up attempts to hit harder targets such as military sites in Britain.
Tehran has rejected accusations of involvement in the Fairford incident or any other accusations of malign activity in Britain, where the authorities have for a number of years accused it of being involved in plots and attempted assassinations against dissidents and Israeli and Jewish targets.
Germany has blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport in August after airport workers found a drone laden with explosives and a detonator at the airport, an important civilian freight and NATO logistics hub in eastern Germany that is also a base for several giant Ukrainian Antonov An-124 cargo planes.

Related:

items.title: 米国株式市場＝Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック続落、エヌビディア巡る不透明感が重し
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　１３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ニューヨーク　１３日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場はＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が続落して取引を終えた。米半導体大手エヌビディアへの懸念がハイテク株を圧迫した。一方、この日発表されたインフレ指標を受け、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が追加利上げに動くとの見方は変わらなかった。

エヌビディアは２％下落し、週間ベースで６週続落。続落期間は２０１２年１０月以来の長さとなった。

英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）によると、エヌビディアの取締役会が、辞任したジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）の後任探しの一環で、英半導体設計大手アームのレネ・ハースＣＥＯに接触したことが分かった。

アメリプライズ・ファイナンシャルのチーフ市場ストラテジスト、アンソニー・サグリムビーン氏は「ハイテク株投資もＡＩ関連株投資も、そしてエヌビディアも、値動きの荒い時期を迎えるだろう。年末まで相場を動かす材料がどう展開するかを巡り、強気派と弱気派がせめぎ合うことになる。信頼感が損なわれた」と述べた。

足元では値動きが荒くなっているものの、主要株価指数は週間では上昇し、ナスダックとＳ＆Ｐ５００はともに４週続いた下落に歯止めをかけた。週間では、Ｓ＆Ｐ５００が２．５１％高、ナスダックが２．２７％高、ダウが２．０７％高となった。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は３．４％下落。アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイシズ（ＡＭＤ）が８．８％安、ブロードコムが４．８％安となり、最大の押し下げ要因となった。

ＡＩ向けクラウドサービスを手掛けるコアウィーブとネビウスも安い。データセンター関連ではＩＲＥＮが６．７％安、アプライド・デジタルが５．８％安となった。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００情報技術株指数は１．７％下落し、Ｓ＆Ｐの主要１１業種の中で最も不振だった。一方、マイクロソフトは序盤の下げを消し、０．２％高で終了した。「アウトルック」や「チームズ」などで発生した世界的な障害が解消に向かい始めた。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を１．２８対１の比率で上回り、ナスダックでも値下がり銘柄数が１．６１対１の比率で上回った。

米取引所の出来高は１６３億８０００万株で、直近２０営業日の平均である１８５億２０００万株を下回った。

items.body:
米国株式市場＝Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック続落、エヌビディア巡る不透明感が重し
6:19 配信

2026年11月13日、ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）　REUTERS/Brendan McDermid（ロイター） ［ニューヨーク　１３日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場はＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が続落して取引を終えた。米半導体大手エヌビディアへの懸念がハイテク株を圧迫した。一方、この日発表されたインフレ指標を受け、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が追加利上げに動くとの見方は変わらなかった。

エヌビディアは２％下落し、週間ベースで６週続落。続落期間は２０１２年１０月以来の長さとなった。

英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）によると、エヌビディアの取締役会が、辞任したジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）の後任探しの一環で、英半導体設計大手アームのレネ・ハースＣＥＯに接触したことが分かった。

アメリプライズ・ファイナンシャルのチーフ市場ストラテジスト、アンソニー・サグリムビーン氏は「ハイテク株投資もＡＩ関連株投資も、そしてエヌビディアも、値動きの荒い時期を迎えるだろう。年末まで相場を動かす材料がどう展開するかを巡り、強気派と弱気派がせめぎ合うことになる。信頼感が損なわれた」と述べた。

足元では値動きが荒くなっているものの、主要株価指数は週間では上昇し、ナスダックとＳ＆Ｐ５００はともに４週続いた下落に歯止めをかけた。週間では、Ｓ＆Ｐ５００が２．５１％高、ナスダックが２．２７％高、ダウが２．０７％高となった。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は３．４％下落。アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイシズ（ＡＭＤ）が８．８％安、ブロードコムが４．８％安となり、最大の押し下げ要因となった。

ＡＩ向けクラウドサービスを手掛けるコアウィーブとネビウスも安い。データセンター関連ではＩＲＥＮが６．７％安、アプライド・デジタルが５．８％安となった。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００情報技術株指数は１．７％下落し、Ｓ＆Ｐの主要１１業種の中で最も不振だった。一方、マイクロソフトは序盤の下げを消し、０．２％高で終了した。「アウトルック」や「チームズ」などで発生した世界的な障害が解消に向かい始めた。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を１．２８対１の比率で上回り、ナスダックでも値下がり銘柄数が１．６１対１の比率で上回った。

米取引所の出来高は１６３億８０００万株で、直近２０営業日の平均である１８５億２０００万株を下回った。

items.title: ＭＳの世界的通信障害収束へ、アウトルックなど約24時間混乱
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１３日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフト（ＭＳ）は１３日、１２日に電子メールサービス「アウトルック」やビジネス向けチャットツール「チームズ」などで発生した世界的な通信障害が収束しつつあると述べた。今回の障害は、約２４時間にわたりオンライン通信を混乱させた。 

同社は、今回の障害はサーバーの問題が原因だとした上で、ソフトウエア修正を広く展開したことでシステムが安定してきていると説明。悪意ある活動は確認していないとし、人工知能（ＡＩ）が原因である可能性も排除したと述べた。

「アウトルック」と「チームズ」は、数億人の利用者を抱える、最も広く利用されている職場向けアプリで、今回の障害により、メールの送信やカレンダー管理、オンライン会議の開催といった重要な業務が妨げられた。 

公式発表によると、今回の障害はオーストラリアや日本から米国に至る各国の政府機関に及び、金融取引会社では業務の遅延が発生、一部企業は決算発表ができなくなり、航空各社は顧客に連絡の遅れを警告する事態となっていた。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Erwin Seba

[ヒューストン １３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Erwin Seba

[ヒューストン １３日 ロイター] - 米国時間の原油先物は下落し、週間ベースでは２週続落の見通しとなった。世界的な供給過剰の拡大を示す兆候が意識されたほか、米政府が9カ月に及ぶ戦争でイランへの封鎖に注力しつつ、経済的な圧力を強めていることも相場の重しとなった。 

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が０．０２ドル（０．０２％）高の１バレル＝９５．８４ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は０．１８ドル（０．２０％）安の８８．５６ドル。

週間ではブレント、ＷＴＩともに約２．５％の下落となる見通し。両指標は前週にそれぞれ１６％、１３％下落していた。

米国とイスラエルによる対イラン戦争に伴う地政学的リスクが低下したことに加え、１３日に発表された国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）の報告書が、世界的な石油の供給過剰の拡大を示唆したことを受け、市場は大きな転換期を迎えている。

プライス・フューチャーズ・グループのシニアアナリスト、フィル・フリン氏は「数カ月前、最大の懸念が供給不足だったことは明らかだ」とし、「今では、最大の懸念は供給過剰のようだ」と述べた。

items.title: US stocks: S&P 500, Nasdaq close lower as Nvidia woes and rate-hike bets pressure US market
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq experienced declines on Friday, primarily driven by concerns surrounding Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. The tech sector faced increased pressure, particularly the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which fell significantly. Although inflation data suggested a slightly lower increase, expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes remained unchanged. Major technology companies, including Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom, contributed to the losses in the sector.
items.body: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended lower on Friday as Nvidia-related concerns weighed on technology stocks, while the latest inflation data did little to change expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes.The S&P lost 31.53 points, or 0.42%, to end at 7,560.87 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 230.13 points, or 0.91%, to 25,135.96. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 46.14 points, or 0.09%, to 52,343.23.Nvidia's shares fell and recorded their sixth straight week of declines, their longest streak since October 2012, after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday. He stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for China. Nvidia’s board has approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Huang, the Financial Times reported.The leadership uncertainty has raised questions about the durability of the AI trade because of Nvidia’s central role in the industry’s expansion and its financial ties to several companies in the sector. AI stocks have been a main driver of the equity bull market.Also Read: Fed officials signal further rate hikes as inflation remains elevated“The tech trade, the AI trade, Nvidia is going to go through a period of volatility, and you’re going to see the bulls and bears kind of wrestle on where this narrative goes through the rest of the year ... there’s been a loss of confidence,” said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial in Troy, Michigan, according to Reuters.“The market and investors are trying to navigate what the AI theme looks like in the absence of Jensen Huang, who was basically the AI champion and willing to use Nvidia’s balance sheet to fund a lot of this AI expansion. That’s gone.”Despite the recent volatility, all three major indexes were on track to post weekly gains. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end four-week losing streaks.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.7%, with Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom among the biggest drags.AI cloud companies CoreWeave and Nebius also declined, while data-centre-related stocks IREN and Applied Digital traded lower.The losses came ahead of Anthropic’s highly anticipated initial public offering next week, which could test demand for established AI companies as investors consider shifting money toward the new entrant.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe S&P 500 technology index fell 1.6%, making it the worst-performing of the benchmark’s 11 major sectors. Microsoft edged 0.4% higher as a global outage affecting products including Outlook and Teams began to ease.The Labor Department said US producer prices rose slightly less than expected in October but increased 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest annual gain since November 2022.The data did little to change expectations for a Federal Reserve rate increase of at least 25 basis points in December. Markets were also pricing in a roughly 10% chance of a larger 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Comments from several Fed officials this week suggested the central bank could consider a more aggressive path of rate increases as inflation pressures intensify.San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said Friday that her “bias” was that the central bank would need to raise its policy rate. Boston Fed President Susan Collins also said tighter monetary policy was coming because inflation remained high.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Fed officials signal further rate hikes as inflation remains elevated
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: Federal Reserve officials are signaling further interest-rate increases to combat persistent inflation pressures in the economy. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly expressed concerns about services inflation and its implications for future policy. Both Boston Fed President Susan Collins and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan emphasized the need for tighter monetary policies. They indicated the possibility of upcoming rate hikes to achieve price stability and mitigate inflation.
items.body: Federal Reserve policymakers signalled that further interest-rate increases are likely as stubborn inflation and rising business costs threaten to keep price pressures elevated, Reuters reported.San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said her “bias” was that the central bank would need to raise its policy rate, particularly because services inflation was moving in the wrong direction and showing signs of persistence.“We’re going to need to, in all likelihood, raise rates; I will deliberate this with my colleagues in December at our meeting and in all future meetings and make the collective decision that we judge is most appropriate for the economy that is evolving,” Daly said at a University of Nevada, Las Vegas Center for Business and Economic Research forecast event.The core Consumer Price Index, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, has risen about 0.3% month over month in each of the past three months. That is well above the monthly increase of 0.2% or less that would be consistent with the Fed’s 2% annual inflation target.Daly said she was particularly concerned that services inflation excluding housing was “not moving in the correct direction,” as that category tends to be persistent.“That’s a place where you might think a retailer, or a professional business, if they have to buy more expensive IT goods, pay higher energy bills and have other inputs that are rising in price, might pass that along to customers,” she added.The Fed raised its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point in September before holding it at a range of 3.75% to 4% in October. Markets widely expect quarter-point increases at the Fed’s December 8-9 and January 26-27 meetings, although Governor Christopher Waller has raised the possibility of a half-point move in December.Daly did not comment specifically on the timing of future increases but said markets understood that the Fed adjusts rates in response to changing economic conditions.She is also monitoring consumer spending closely ahead of the December meeting.Collins sees tighter policy aheadBoston Fed President Susan Collins also said further tightening was needed because inflation remained high, suggesting that rates may have to rise more than she previously expected.“I think it’s clear the direction that monetary policy needs to go and I would think that soon some additional firming, tightening of policy is appropriate,” Collins said in an interview with Bloomberg Television.Recent inflation data have been unfavourable and indicate that price pressures are spreading across the economy, Collins said. “I think it may be that a bit of a tighter policy path than I had pencilled in a couple of months ago might be appropriate.”Collins declined to specify how quickly rates should rise or how high they should go.“I don’t want to get ahead in terms of how high we should go or how fast,” Collins said, adding that her “best-case scenario” is for “a careful adjustment of policy.” She acknowledged, however, that “there are scenarios where I might think about that somewhat differently.”Speaking while attending a housing conference hosted by the Boston Fed, Collins said restoring price stability was essential to a healthy housing sector, even if tighter policy caused some near-term pain. She also said financial markets appeared to be functioning well.Logan calls for stronger market-support toolsDallas Fed President Lorie Logan said inflation was too high and monetary policy needed to become more restrictive. Earlier in the week, she argued for at least two additional quarter-point rate increases, potentially in quick succession.Logan also said the US Treasury market was functioning “very well” despite bouts of interest-rate volatility and that banks had improved their access to emergency funding over the past three years.However, she called on the Fed to strengthen its tools for supporting Treasury-market functioning and providing liquidity to banks without working against monetary policy.“Especially in an economic environment where tighter policy appears necessary, I believe it is prudent for the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) to strengthen its tools for supporting market functioning without providing unnecessary economic stimulus,” Logan said at a Dallas Fed conference on bank funding.Logan, a former head of open-market operations at the New York Fed, said no intervention was currently needed. She warned, however, that intervening during a monetary-policy tightening cycle could complicate the Fed’s communications.“Historically, the Fed’s interventions to support market functioning have come at times when the FOMC also wanted to stimulate economic activity,” she said. “The same asset purchases could serve two purposes: providing monetary policy accommodation and supporting market liquidity.”“If Treasury market dysfunction emerged now, the FOMC would not have the luxury of using the same asset purchases to accomplish two goals,” Logan said.Logan further said that the banks had improved their access to contingent funding, which provides liquidity during periods of market stress, but should continue preparing to use facilities such as the Fed’s discount window.As services such as FedNow and private-sector payment systems expand, banks could face liquidity needs during weekends and holidays. With the Fed planning to extend its Fedwire Funds wholesale payment system to Sundays and weekday holidays, Logan said discount-window operations should also be expanded.“This is not a change any one Reserve Bank can make on its own,” she said. “I look forward to discussions with my colleagues about this possibility.”Logan also urged the Fed to develop the ability to centrally clear its repurchase, or repo, operations. “This would reduce the balance sheet costs of intermediation,” she said. “Funding from the Fed could then flow more efficiently to the broad market.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

Both Boston Fed President Susan Collins and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan emphasized the need for tighter monetary policies. They indicated the possibility of upcoming rate hikes to achieve price stability and mitigate inflation.

FAST

WASHINGTON, Nov 13 : Risks tied to the artificial intelligence sector surged to become the top-cited concern for financial stability, according to a semi-annual report released by the Federal Reserve on Friday.
The US central bank's Financial Stability Report found potential risks from the technology itself and the breakneck investment in the sector as the preeminent concern of survey respondents. Eighty-seven percent of contacts surveyed cited AI as a salient risk to the financial system, as respondents pointed to worries about cyberattacks, risks associated with complex forms of AI-related financing, and the possibility of an AI earnings slowdown spurring a broad market correction. Just 50 per cent of those surveyed cited AI as a risk in the May version of the Fed's survey.
Other top concerns cited in the survey also had heavy AI implications. The second most-cited concern was regarding a broad correction in risk assets at 52 per cent of those surveyed, and cyberattacks specifically were flagged as a worry by 43 per cent of respondents. Forty-eight percent of those surveyed also fretted about higher long-term interest rates, while 43 per cent cited fiscal debt sustainability as a worry.
The survey was conducted in September and October, meaning respondents weighed in before the latest turmoil at chipmaker Nvidia, where CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving Chinese businesswoman whom the New York Times has reported is under suspicion as a Chinese spy. The survey also preceded the results of recent midterm elections in which the American public's rising concerns about AI were also a central issue.

The increased focus on AI was underpinned by the report itself, as the Fed devoted a chunk of the report to examining the rapid increase in debt issuance tied to data centers and other advanced computing infrastructure. The Fed report found that advanced computing-related debt issuance had surged to $680 billion by October 2026, already a fivefold increase on debt issued in all of 2023. Advanced computing-related borrowing now accounts for nearly a third of all nonfinancial investment-grade corporate debt issuance, after amounting to less than 6 per cent three years ago.
The Fed noted in its report that the rapid influx of debt issuance and investment in AI-related infrastructure could be compared to the broadband telecom investment cycle of the late 1990s, although the Fed said it is possible the current investment cycle may soon surpass that era. And the central bank focused on the complex financing arrangements underpinning some of this investment, noting that arrangements like long-term contracts, leases and guarantees allow hyperscalers and other large firms to support financing such projects by smaller third parties, and graphics card designers and hyperscalers often further contribute to investments via equity.
Data collected by the Fed found that debt, guarantees, and not-yet-commenced leases on this infrastructure could exceed $3 trillion.
The Fed said such "circular financing" dynamics could allow the largest firms to absorb losses in the event of a downturn, minimizing the impact on the broader financial system. However, it could also mean that those firms' exposure to such a downturn could be "substantially larger" than indicated by their on-balance-sheet liabilities.
"The complex interlinkages among firms engaged in the data center buildout, public credit markets, private lenders, and special purpose financing vehicles create vulnerabilities that necessitate close monitoring," the report stated.
Elsewhere in the financial system, the Fed found that asset valuations across a range of classes remained high, due in part to investor enthusiasm about AI. The report noted that investment in the AI sector has been a significant driver of US economic growth this year, and an unexpected downturn in corporate earnings could prompt a market decline, tighter credit, and reduced investment, which would all weigh on the economy.
Such a downturn could also be exacerbated by relatively high levels of leverage in some portions of the financial sector. The Fed noted in its level that leverage among hedge funds, particularly the largest firms, remains at the highest levels recorded since they began gathering such data in 2013.

Source: Reuters

items.title: ハセットＮＥＣ委員長退任の報道、後任にベセント氏ら浮上　政権は否定
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン １３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン １３日 ロイター] - 米ホワイトハウスは１３日、ケビン・ハセット国家経済会議（ＮＥＣ）委員長が今後数週間以内にトランプ政権を離れるとの報道を否定した。

米ニュースサイトのセマフォーは同日これに先立ち、計画を知る関係者３人の話として、ハセット氏が今後数週間以内に退任すると報じた。報道によると、ハセット氏は１１月３日の中間選挙より前から政権外での役職について打診していた。中間選挙では民主党が米連邦議会の上下両院を奪還し、共和党のトランプ大統領にとって打撃となった。セマフォーは、ハセット氏の退任は選挙結果とは関係がないとしている。

セマフォーによると、ハセット氏の後任候補には、両方の役職を兼務する可能性があるベセント財務長官や、同長官の顧問を務めるデービッド・ザーボス氏が挙がっている。ハセット氏の計画は変わる可能性もあるという。

ＣＮＢＣによると、ハセット委員長は、ホワイトハウスを退任するとの報道について「事実ではない」と述べた。

ホワイトハウス当局者も「この報道には事実に基づく根拠がない。ハセット氏はトランプ大統領の経済チームの主要メンバーであり、引き続き大統領の経済政策の推進に取り組む」と述べた。

米財務省は、コメントの要請に直ちには応じなかった。

ハセット氏は、トランプ氏の第１次政権でホワイトハウスの大統領経済諮問委員会（ＣＥＡ）委員長を務めた。

２０１９年に同職を退いたが、その後ホワイトハウスに復帰し、新型コロナウイルスのパンデミック（世界的大流行）の間、トランプ氏の上級顧問を務めた。

ハセット氏は、パウエル連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）前議長の後任候補と目されていたが、最終的にはウォーシュ氏がその職に起用された。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種公益事業株指数は１．１６％高。電力・ガス大手セントリカは３．８％上昇した。

保険会社アビバは３．４％高。堅調な保険料収入が確認され、買われた。

来週は、英消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）や雇用統計が発表される予定。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞ 小動き。ただ、堅調な業績発表に加え、ハイテク株から投資資金を移す動きを受け、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は週間ベースで２．４４％高と、6月下旬以来の好成績となった。

ＳＴＯＸＸユーロ圏銀行株指数も週間で４．２３％上昇した。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種テクノロジー株指数は前日比１．２５％安。ドイツの半導体大手インフィニオン・テクノロジーズは４．３％、半導体製造装置メーカー、アイクストロンは４．７％、フランスの配電・制御機器大手シュナイダー・エレクトリックは０．６％いずれも下落した。

スイスの高級ブランド、リシュモンは３．８％安。一方、国際送金を手がけるワイズは７．７％高。大幅増収決算を発表し、買われた。

ゴールドマン・サックスは、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数の１年先の目標を７００ポイントに引き上げた。ユーロ圏の２０２６年第３・四半期（２６年７－９月期）の域内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は前期比０．４％増だった。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

ドイツ国債利回りが週間ベースで２カ月ぶりの大幅上昇となる見通しとなった。予想を上回る米インフレ指標を受けて、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の利上げ観測が高まる一方、株式相場の反発が安全資産への需要を抑制した。

先週のハイテク株の急落を受け、安全資産である国債に投資家の買いが殺到した。１３日は世界的に株価が下落し、ハイテク比率の高いナスダック１００は大幅安となった。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは４ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の３．３７％。週間ベースでは１１ｂｐ上昇の見通し。先週６日には８月２６日以来の低水準となる３．２０７５％を付けていた。

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは２ｂｐ低下の３．１０９％。ただ、週間ベースでは１３ｂｐの上昇となる見通し。

ＥＣＢのユーロ圏短期金利（ＥＳＴＲ）フォワードレートによると、預金金利は２０２７年終盤までに、現行の２．５０％から約３．２５％に上昇すると見込まれている。先週終盤時点では３％だった。また、同年１２月までに預金金利は２．７４％になるとみられている。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は１５４ｂｐと７ｂｐ拡大した。ただ、週間では８ｂｐの縮小となる見通し。１０月２２日には１７７．７ｂｐと、ユーロ圏債務危機が最も深刻だった２０１１年１１月半ば以来の高水準を付けた。

items.title: 英仏独など欧州5カ国とＥＵ、ウクライナ和平交渉に参加へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Padraic Halpin　Graham Fahy

[ダブリン １３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Padraic Halpin　Graham Fahy

[ダブリン １３日 ロイター] - 欧州連合（ＥＵ）のコスタ大統領は１３日、米国が仲介する次回のロシアとウクライナの和平交渉に、ＥＵに加え、英国、フランス、ドイツ、イタリア、ポーランドの５カ国の代表が参加することで合意したと発表した。

コスタ大統領は非公式首脳会議後、記者会見で「ウクライナの未来と欧州大陸の安全保障を左右するあらゆる議論において、欧州は明確かつ統一された声で発言しなければならない」と語った。

トランプ米政権のウィットコフ特使は１２日、ロシアのプーチン大統領がウクライナ和平協議の次回会合に欧州の代表が参加することに同意したと明らかにしていた。

EU当局者によると、欧州の代表は、５カ国の国家安全保障担当顧問に加え、ＥＵの執行機関である欧州委員会、および欧州理事会の代表者らとなる公算が大きい。

また、北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）も代表を派遣するとみられる。

items.title: Investor Outlook: AI helps accelerate quantum computing development
items.author: BNN Bloomberg
items.summary: Xanadu CEO Christian Weedbrook discusses Canada’s quantum computing ambitions, third-quarter results and the path to commercial growth.
items.body: Canada’s quantum computing ambitions are drawing attention to the country’s ability to turn research into a globally competitive industry. The federal budget has put the sector’s future in sharper focus. BNN Bloomberg spoke with Christian Weedbrook, founder and CEO at Xanadu, about Canada’s position in quantum computing, the company’s third-quarter results and its development plans. Key Takeaways Read the full transcript below: ROGER: Last week’s federal budget singled out Xanadu by name as a critical investment alongside Cohere for Canada to maintain its sovereignty. Let’s find out what it will take for companies like Xanadu to scale and compete on the global stage. Joining me now is Christian Weedbrook, the founder and CEO of Xanadu. Christian, good to see you. How are you? CHRISTIAN: I’m good, thank you. How are you? ROGER: Good. Let’s talk big picture. Being mentioned in a budget, a lot of pressure on you. Where do you see quantum fitting in? People are starting to grasp AI. I think quantum, though, is still, is still the next level. Where do you see it fitting in now and coming down the road? CHRISTIAN: Yeah, it was great to see Xanadu mentioned in the budget, as you mentioned. You know, I think the big thing that more and more people are realizing is the fact that, you know, quantum is going to be the next big thing after artificial intelligence. Folks are now very much familiar with AI and what it can do, and we see, you know, quantum computing as the next big thing after AI, and specifically, like something, if you look at the early days of the internet or early days of digital computing, that’s really where quantum computing sits. Xanadu is one of the leaders in the world, proudly Canadian, and we truly are on the world stage. ROGER: And where does it fit in with AI? Is it competition, or is it going to work together with it? CHRISTIAN: Really, we see it as working together, for sure. You know, along with it being the next big thing after AI, AI is not going anywhere. And to give you a great example, we use a lot of AI currently in building towards building a large-scale quantum computer. Some of the AI LLMs that we’ve used have really sped up our team’s progress by a year or more, which is quite phenomenal. So they go very well together, and we think that’s an, you know, really essential component to getting to a large-scale quantum computer that can really attract large amount of customers and, at that point, change the world. ROGER: And what would it mean for sovereignty here in Canada? CHRISTIAN: Yeah, I think that’s one of the reasons why we were mentioned in the budget. It’s a sovereign play. It’s really important. Specifically, we’re in the DARPA QBI program. Canada has its own version of the QBI program called the Canadian Quantum Champions Program, and that’s, I believe, what was mentioned in the budget. So the Canadian government has long invested in quantum computing through universities, probably for over two decades now, and Xanadu and other great companies in Canada are now leveraging that, you know, that seed that was planted in terms of the jobs. We had nearly 400 folks. Half of them, I believe, now, or over half, are actually from Canada. So we’ve done a great job in attracting the future workforce and talent by coming to Canada and staying here. ROGER: Is Canada, is Canada a centre for quantum? And are they keeping people? You say some people have come, but are we losing some as well? CHRISTIAN: No, I mean, on the overall, we’re definitely attracting the talent and keeping them here. They love Canada. They love the fact that, you know, that we have some world-class talent. Three of the Canadian companies, including Xanadu, are actually part of 11 companies in the DARPA QBI program. So we’re hitting a well above our body weight, and also funding. We have a lot of great investors that are investing, Canadian investors, and so I think that’s attracting some great talent. But overall, I think it’s, you know, Xanadu has had four Nature publications, two in the last year, and really the best talent want to see what the best talent is working on and come join them. And Xanadu is a great example of that. ROGER: And talking about where you’re at, I mean, your earnings report just came out, some big misses. What’s driving all that right now? I know you’re early. CHRISTIAN: Yeah, yeah, exactly. The main thing that we focus on is hardware development and hardware milestones and achieving them. And so, the biggest challenge for us and anyone else building quantum computers is errors. And we’re a photonic-based approach, and the errors really come from a loss and the loss of the photonic systems, essentially. So we focus on taking the opportunity for our earnings calls to reiterate that it’s all about technical milestones. Revenue is obviously key, but quantum computing is really the end result, is achieving a large-scale quantum computer by 2029, 2030. Other companies are doing great work, and they’re focusing, it seems like, some cases exclusively on revenue. We believe that, for us, the best approach is to focus on hardware milestones because in 2029, 2030, when we’re aiming to have our large-scale quantum computer, that’s when all bets are off, and that’s when true revenue actually occurs. And we think investors are investing in us because of our hardware milestones, our technical capabilities and our unique photonic-based approach. ROGER: And how are you doing with those milestones? What are you hitting right now? CHRISTIAN: Yeah, our milestones are on track. We announced three key optical loss demonstrations, and particularly we have what we believe is the world’s best low-loss optical switch. Optical switches are needed for our quantum computer, but they have far bigger, you know, currently far bigger applications in, in quant— in, in AI and data centres as well. So we’re really excited about that, and that’s a great example of where the team is hitting their hardware milestones when it comes to loss reduction. ROGER: Is that a possible revenue stream, then? Data centres before you, we get into the full quantum computers. CHRISTIAN: It is a possibility. As we mentioned on our earnings call, our relationship to revenue is as long as it doesn’t deviate from building a large-scale quantum computer, which is what our main focus is, then we’re definitely open to commercializing things. The reality is, Xanadu has, you know, arguably the best team in the world for extreme low-loss optical components. Things like AI, data centres, they’re becoming more and more relevant. So we do keep an eye on that, and it’s something that we’re definitely considering. ROGER: And what are some of the other milestones that you’ve been hitting, and what do they mean? CHRISTIAN: Yeah, some great partnerships. We announced partnerships with ASML. We believe we’re the only quantum company so far that’s actually working with ASML. We announced great partnerships with Bluefors as well, and all of these partnerships are helping us to achieve the ultimate vision of a large-scale quantum computer. Also, from the commercial side and partnerships and revenue side, some great partnerships with Mitsubishi as well. So the team is firing on all cylinders. I’m really excited of the future. ROGER: OK, Christian, thank you very much for joining us today. Appreciate it. CHRISTIAN: Thank you for having me. ROGER: Christian Weedbrook is the founder and CEO of Xanadu. --- This BNN Bloomberg summary and transcript of the Nov. 13, 2026 interview with Christian Weedbrook are published with the assistance of AI. Original research, interview questions and added context was created by BNN Bloomberg journalists. items.title: ゴールドマン、Ｓ＆Ｐ５００今後1年で8700に上昇と予想　割安感など追い風
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１３日 ロイター] - 米ゴールドマン・サックスは１２日付けのリポートで、米国の代表的な株価指数であるＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種指数が今後１年間で８７００ポイントまで上昇するとの予想を明らかにした。１２日の終値７５９２．４０と比べ、約１５％の上昇を見込む。最近の相場下落を受けて割安感が出ているほか、米経済の底堅さや、債券利回りやインフレ低下などが追い風になると見ている。

３日の米中間選挙で野党民主党が勝利し、人工知能（ＡＩ）データセンター関連投資減速への懸念が高まったことで、ハイテク株に売り圧力が生じた。ゴールドマンは、投資の減速はＡＩインフラ関連部門全体の業績の圧迫要因になるとみる。

２０２７年に世界の主要企業の増益率は少なくとも半減すると予想。米国はハイパースケーラー（大規模クラウド事業者）が設備投資を抑制することで、増益率が足元の３６％から１１％に下がると見込んだ。

こうした状況を踏まえ、ゴールドマンは「株式はプラスのリターンを生むと予想するが、ここ数年よりも変動が大きくなるだろう」と指摘した。株式市場別の投資判断では、米国と日本は「オーバーウエート」、アジアと新興市場は「中立」、欧州は「アンダーウエート」の評価を維持した。

items.title: 米ＳＦ連銀総裁、追加利上げ必要との見方　サービスインフレを懸念
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１３日 ロイター] - 米サンフランシスコ地区連銀のデイリー総裁は１３日、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が利上げする必要があるというのが自身の「見方」だと述べた。特にサービス部門のインフレが「正しい方向に動いていない」ことや、インフレ高進を示す兆候が見られることを理由とした。

デイリー総裁は、ネバダ大学ラスベガス校の経済見通しイベントで、「われわれは、おそらく利上げが必要になるだろう」と述べ、「生産者からは、利益率から吸収できる余地がなくなりつつあり、これを消費者に転嫁することを真剣に検討したいという声がますます多く聞かれている。われわれが回避したいのは、こうしたインフレ圧力だ」と述べた。

デイリー氏は、他の複数の政策当局者と同様に、住宅を除くサービスインフレが「正しい方向に動いていない」ことを特に懸念していると指摘。この部分のインフレは粘着性があるため、特に厄介だとした。

「小売業者や専門業者が、より高価なＩＴ機器を買わざるを得なくなり、光熱費や他の投入コストも上昇しているとすれば、その分を顧客に転嫁しようとするかもしれない」と述べた。  

デイリー氏はまた、米経済の大半を占める個人消費にも注視していると指摘。「個人消費は驚くほど底堅く推移しており、まだ落ち込みは見られない」とし、特に年末商戦期における消費者動向に注目していると述べた。

items.title: ＣＯＰ３１、化石燃料巡る対立色濃く　合意形成へ課題浮き彫り
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [アンタルヤ（トルコ）　１３日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[アンタルヤ（トルコ）　１３日　ロイター] - トルコで開催中の第３１回国連気候変動枠組み条約締約国会議（ＣＯＰ３１）で、化石燃料を巡る各国の対立が色濃くなっている。オブザーバーらは１３日、主要な化石燃料生産・消費国から、新たな具体的目標の明記や、化石燃料からの脱却で合意することへの反対意見が出ていると明らかにし、２週間にわたる会合での合意形成に向けた課題が浮き彫りになりつつある。

各国との折衝役を担うオーストラリアは、議長国トルコと共に地球温暖化による悪影響に対処するための合意成立に努めている。開幕後の数日間、合意で採択される政治文書の内容について意見を収集し、来週初めには草案の策定を目指している。

一方、サウジアラビアやロシアなどの主要産油国は、化石燃料を制限する文言に抵抗。また、インドなど開発途上国は、自国の発展やエネルギー源を制限しかねない措置に反対している。

トルコは、化石燃料を直接燃やすのではなく、電力を使うことへと置き換える「電化」の拡大を合意の中心とするよう提案。化石燃料からの脱却加速が排出量の削減につながると主張している。欧州連合（ＥＵ）代表団のトップは、電化目標を支持。ブラジルなどは、明確な移行計画策定の義務化を提唱している。主要な石油消費国、米国はＣＯＰ３１を欠席している。

環境団体Ｅ３Ｇのオブザーバーは、それぞれが自国の立場を強く主張しているとしつつ、この段階ではよくあることだと指摘した。

items.body:
China and Thailand should support each other on issues of core interest and major concern, and deepen cooperation in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, finance and clean energy, China’s Premier Li Qiang told Thailand’s prime minister in Bangkok on Friday.

China was willing to import more quality products from Thailand and encouraged Chinese companies to invest in the country, Li told Thailand’s Anutin Charnvirakul, according to China’s official Xinhua news agency.

The two sides should step up efforts in combating illegal and criminal activities and deepen cooperation in China’s flagship Belt and Road infrastructure initiative, including advancing a rail link connecting Thailand with China, Li said according to the official Chinese summary of the meeting.

WASHINGTON, Nov 13 : Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang turned to law firm Paul Weiss amid his rapid fall this week, tapping a firm that reached a controversial deal with President Donald Trump last year and whose own longtime leader was forced to step down in February.
Huang resigned on Thursday after more than 30 years leading the top AI chipmaker, following reports that he had extramarital affairs with three women, including an Nvidia executive and Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy.
Paul Weiss, Nvidia and a spokesperson for Huang had no immediate comment on Friday about the nature of the law firm's work for Huang.
New-York based Paul Weiss, with more than 1,500 lawyers, long has been a go-to for corporate boards and executives facing regulatory scrutiny, misconduct allegations or other reputational crises.

It built a reputation pairing lucrative work for Citigroup and other business clients with liberal advocacy and fundraising for Democratic candidates, including Kamala Harris.
But the firm drew sharp criticism within the legal profession and from Democrats last year after striking a deal with Trump to rescind an executive order the Republican president issued against it in March 2025.
Trump's order suspended security clearances for the firm's lawyers and restricted their access to government buildings and officials, citing its internal diversity policies and its association with a prosecutor who investigated the president.
Paul Weiss pledged in its settlement to dedicate $40 million in pro bono legal services to support "mutually agreed" projects with the White House, sparking similar deals by eight other law firms. Its longtime chairman Brad Karp defended the accord, calling Trump's order an existential threat. 
The tumult facing Karp ramped up early this year, after emails surfaced showing Karp's extensive personal and business communications with the late convicted sex offender and financier Jeffrey Epstein.
Karp resigned from his leadership post in February, saying the reports about Epstein had created a distraction that was not in the firm's interests. He has not been accused of wrongdoing.
GO-TO FIRM FOR CORPORATE CRISES
Paul Weiss has a stable of former senior Justice Department officials and others who frequently step in for clients when crisis strikes.
BlackRock in 2021 hired partner Loretta Lynch, who was US Attorney General under President Barack Obama, to assist with an internal probe of former employees' claims of sexual harassment and discrimination.
Huang is working with Paul Weiss partners Melinda Haag and Walter Brown, the New York Times reported on Thursday. Haag served as US attorney in San Francisco during the Obama administration. She and Brown did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not independently confirm which lawyers at the firm are representing Huang.
The Republican leaders of several US House committees, including Foreign Affairs, addressed a letter to Brown on Thursday stating they wish to interview Huang in closed-door session next month.
Haag successfully defended former Fitbit executive Katherine Mogal, who was acquitted in 2020 of federal charges alleging theft of trade secrets from a rival wearable-device maker. Brown is on the team defending Meta Platforms in a lawsuit by an Australian mining magnate over scam ads on Facebook showing him promoting fake cryptocurrency.
Nvidia’s board has hired another top firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Kratz to conduct an independent investigation. That probe will be led by Wachtell’s Joon Kim, a former senior federal prosecutor in Manhattan.

Source: Reuters

Nov 13 : Jensen Huang as a Bollywood matinee idol, as a character from "The Matrix" or donning a red velvet suit on a poster for an alternate-universe version of "The Spy Who Shagged Me": the Nvidia co-founder's extramarital affairs, including with a Chinese businesswoman, set the Internet afire this week.
The storm of AI generated video and images, many of the clips were likely made with the help of Nvidia graphics chips, provided some light relief to a scandal that toppled one of the tech industry's most prominent CEOs, wiping out hundreds of billions of investor value and triggering investigations worldwide.
The Huang memes competed for the spotlight with a raft of comedic takes on the more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft services including Outlook and Teams, topping off a week that kicked off with the latest Stephen Miller vampire memes after U.S. President Donald Trump named him as chief of staff, effective Monday.
But it was humor on the crisis surrounding Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia that dominated many social media feeds, with many of the clips likely made using Nvidia graphics chips, RaviKunvariyaX quipped on X.

"Jensen is literally funding the infrastructure, selling the hardware, and collecting revenue while the internet uses his own technology to troll him," the user said.
One widely shared image showed Jensen Huang in an Nvidia shirt turning away from logos for AI models including OpenAI, Google's Gemini and DeepSeek, then pointing at a woman labeled "Chinese Model," a play on the allegations surrounding his resignation. 
A satire on X placed Jensen Huang and Alice Huang's faces over those of actors in the opening credits of the classic sit-com "Three's Company," about a man with two female roommates.
Others included an AI-generated video with millions of views featuring US President Donald Trump, along others depicting what ostensibly happened behind the scenes at the chip giant. Nvidia was among the trending topics in popular platforms such as Reddit and X for most of this week.
A more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft services, including Outlook and Teams, that sent some business scrambling for fax machines, phones and paper added fresh fodder for the meme factories late in the week.
'HAPPY FRIDAY'
"No rush. Take your time ... Happy Friday," read one widely shared post, signed "Every corporate employee," X user omgsidewalks posted. The X post was viewed over 4 million times.
Other memes imagined a role for Microsoft's much maligned 'Clippy' 90s-era virtual helper either causing or explaining the outage.
Microsoft's services have been a repeat meme subject, including after a global IT outage in 2024 triggered by a faulty CrowdStrike update, that crashed Windows machines.
"every year, microsoft should turn off outlook for an afternoon so we can all go outside and play with out friends :)," read another X post with thousands of views.

items.title: Nvidia crisis: Senate panel summons Jensen Huang, Howard Lutnick to testify
items.author: Agencies
items.summary: Senior US officials are discussing Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's possible exit as lawmakers question the administration's oversight of advanced AI chip exports to China ...
items.body: Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee as Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy raises national security concerns. Senator Tim Scott, Republican of South Carolina, on Thursday evening sent letters to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. “Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive United States (US) technology,” Scott said in a social media post, adding, “The American people deserve answers.”  Congressional leaders of both political parties have said they support efforts to hear from Huang directly about his entanglement with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who US officials concluded had been recruited by China’s main spy agency. Scott asked Huang to appear on December 3 by his own volition but also threatened that the committee could issue a subpoena. House Republicans also said on Thursday they were in discussions with Huang to testify before other committees. Huang has hired lawyers who previously represented executives in government investigations, according to people familiar with the matter. Senior White House officials are discussing whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out amid a spy scandal surrounding Nvidia’s now-former CEO Jensen Huang, two people familiar with the situation said on Thursday. A growing number of lawmakers criticised Lutnick for the administration’s refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a key US trade blacklist, and over whether the government was properly overseeing Nvidia’s exports to China. Criticism of Lutnick’s actions predates Thursday’s resignation of Huang, who said he would step down as chief executive officer (CEO) of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) chipmaker after reports of an affair with Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. But the charge that Lutnick has not done enough to restrict AI chip shipments to China has emerged as the fallout from Jensen Huang’s actions grows. Earlier on Thursday, a White House official said President Donald Trump “maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position.” In June, Reuters reported the Trump administration had held off adding China’s AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and over 100 other firms flagged as national security risks to a trade blacklist. Asked on CNN if Lutnick should lose his job, Republican Senator John Kennedy said: “I don’t know yet.” He and others have urged Lutnick to quickly publicly answer questions and noted he will be called to appear before Congress. “This is as serious as an aneurism.” The US has not posted any additions to that list since October 2025, the longest stretch between new postings in over a decade. Reuters earlier reported that the US Commerce Department has not added new Chinese companies to that list for fear of escalating tensions between the US and China. Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat, who will chair the Senate Banking Committee starting in January, and incoming Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chair Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, wrote to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, telling the administration to preserve all documents related to Nvidia’s exports of advanced AI chips to China. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday his department had favored putting Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed on the US entity list for months but it was up to the Commerce Department to act, adding that the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) could possibly take other action. He added that the administration was working to shut down “leakage” in the chip export system.

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on sidelines of APEC
items.summary: While the leaders gathering for joint talks will mark a singular moment, analysts say expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs ...
items.body:
Home / World News / Trump, Xi, Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on sidelines of APEC

Trump, Xi, Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on sidelines of APEC While the leaders gathering for joint talks will mark a singular moment, analysts say expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs

A worker pushes a row of trolleys past a promotion board for the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' meeting at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport, in Shenzhen, China | Image: Reuters

AP Washington 6 min read Last Updated : Nov 14 2026 | 7:53 AM IST

Listen to This Article

The leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet Thursday on the sidelines of next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's biggest nuclear powers.
While the leaders gathering for joint talks will mark a singular moment, analysts say expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs, and they will be heavier in symbolism than substance.
Plans for the three-way summit with Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin were confirmed on Friday by the White House. It comes at a complicated moment in relations between the three countries.
 

Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the US war with Iran and other tensions between the world's foremost economic powers.
Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly five-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.

Five things to know about APEC as Trump, Putin and Xi set to attend summit

The US president has insisted that such a meeting would provide an opportunity for the three leaders to discuss the US war with Iran and his goal of reaching a three-way agreement on their nuclear arms stockpiles.

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty -- known as New START -- expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for "a new, improved and modernised" deal that includes China.
But Beijing's arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the US and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With US and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.

Beijing was least certain about the value of the summit By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China's growing clout and prestige.
"I would be shocked if there were a joint statement that came out of this meeting that said anything about denuclearisation," said Edgard Kagan, a former US ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.
"I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signalling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they're making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don't like," Kagan said.

The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.
More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China's argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia's war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran.

The trilateral meeting could undercut China's push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University.
"You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism," he said.
The leaders have met in pairs plenty of times over the years Putin and Xi are no strangers. They've fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as "dear friend."   Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025. Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi.

Beijing is the Number one trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022.
As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia, China increased its purchases of Russia's energy resources and became Moscow's principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries. Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies.
In the lead-up to Russia's war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a "no-limits friendship." China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv's Western allies played a part in provoking Russia's military action in Ukraine.

Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing's policy on issues related to Taiwan.
Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel. The U.S. leader has blamed surging energy prices on Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv's back.
Planning for the summit has drawn comparisons to the Yalta Conference, the 1945 gathering at which leaders of the US, Britain and the Soviet Union agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four military occupation zones and finalised plans for establishing the United Nations.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has dismissed the Yalta comparisons, noting that any potential agreements reached in Shenzhen can't be enforced on others.
"It's clear that a meeting between the leaders of countries such as Russia, China and the United States is extremely significant," Peskov said. "However, let's not forget that the vision for a global order is that no one tries to impose any particular view of global order, and it should be based entirely on mutual benefit and mutual respect.

items.title: マイクロソフト障害、ＩＴ大手への依存浮き彫り　電話やファクスで急場しのぐ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Iain Withers　Liang-sa Loh　Inti Landauro

[ロンドン／台北／パリ １３日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフト の「Ｍｉｃｒｏｓｏｆｔ
items.body:
Iain Withers　Liang-sa Loh　Inti Landauro

[ロンドン／台北／パリ １３日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフト の「Ｍｉｃｒｏｓｏｆｔ ３６５」や「アウトルック」などで世界規模の障害が発生し、数百万人がメールを利用できなくなった問題は、世界の商取引や公共サービス、通信が少数のテクノロジー企業にいかに依存しているかを改めて浮き彫りにした。

長時間に及ぶ障害は、マイクロソフトの「チームズ」や「コパイロット」にも波及。銀行やトレーダーから海運会社まで、世界の大手企業などに影響が広がった。大半は基幹システムが稼働を続けていると報告したが、一部では取引や事務作業が滞った。電話やファクス、ブルートゥースといった従来の技術を復活させて急場をしのいだ利用者もいた。

調査会社ＰＰフォーサイトのアナリスト、パオロ・ペスカトーレ氏は「緊急時対応計画に投資し、必要な時に代替手段が実際に機能するか検証するよう求める圧力が強まっている」と述べた。通信やデータ保存といった重要サービスでは、複数の事業者を利用する必要があると指摘した。

マイクロソフトは、原因はサーバーの問題だと説明し、悪意ある活動は把握していないとした。同社のウェブサイトによると、「３６５」サービスの利用者は４億３０００万人を超える。

マイクロソフトは１３日の最新の状況説明で、サービスの安定的な復旧に向けて修正措置をより広範囲に適用した結果、安定化の兆しが見られるとした。

パリ、ブリュッセル、ミラノなどで複数の証券取引所を運営する欧州のユーロネクストは、上場企業に電話での連絡を呼びかけた。広報担当者は「状況に対処し、増加した業務を処理できるよう、チームの対応能力を十分に確保した」と説明。機密性や情報の完全性を守るため、電話をかけてきた人の本人確認を行っているとした。

１３日に決算を発表した英保険大手アビバは、代替策を講じたと説明した。決算説明会用の別の電話番号を案内したほか、電子メールが使えないため、録音データの転送にブルートゥースを利用した。

同社のアマンダ・ブラン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）はロイターに対し、約２週間前に最重要の技術システムで同規模の障害が起きることを想定した訓練を実施していたと語った。

海運大手マースクは、緊急の用件は電話で連絡するよう顧客に要請。障害に関して予期しない連絡を受けた場合は、現地の担当者に真偽を確認するよう求めた。

台湾では証券会社や生命保険会社、投資信託会社の資金運用に支障が出た。関係者の１人によると、別の金融会社では、通常は電子メールで確認する短期手形などの取引について、代わりにファクスで確認した。

あるトレーダーによると、台湾の外国金融機関は特に大きな影響を受けた。多くのデータをマイクロソフトのシステム経由で海外の本社に電子メールで送信しているためだ。

英国では、ＨＳＢＣとバークレイズが影響を調べるため、社内の障害対応チームを始動させた。電子メールシステムは停止したものの、大半の顧客向けサービスに影響はなかった。

関係者の１人によると、ＨＳＢＣは職員に対し、障害を回避するために個人の電子メールや「ワッツアップ」など、承認されていない連絡手段を使わないよう改めて注意を促した。

取引業務に携わる２人は、１３日に一部市場で取引量の減少が見られたと述べ、取引の執行が難しくなったことが原因との見方を示した。

リスク管理会社コントロール・リスクスのケイトリン・イーゲン氏は、世界的な大企業は通常、緊急時対応計画を備えているものの、主要サービスの突然の停止は、それでも「警鐘」になると指摘した。

items.title: Microsoft outage eases after over a day, recovery timeline uncertain
items.summary: Microsoft said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant and that a broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing the system ...
items.body:
Home / World News / Microsoft outage eases after over a day, recovery timeline uncertain

Microsoft outage eases after over a day, recovery timeline uncertain Microsoft said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant and that a broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing the system

Microsoft services, including Teams, Outlook, Copilot and several Microsoft 365 applications, affecting users worldwide on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026.(Photo:PTI)

Reuters 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 14 2026 | 7:38 AM IST

Listen to This Article

A global outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams was easing on Friday after more than 24 hours of disruption crippled online communications across businesses and governments, though the company said it still had no timeline for full recovery of services.
Microsoft said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant and that a broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing the system. It said it was not aware of any malicious activity and ruled out AI as the cause.
Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings.
 

It affected government agencies from Australia and Japan to the United States, caused delays at trading firms, hindered some companies from publishing earnings and prompted airlines to warn customers of communication lags, according to public statements.
Organizations that host Microsoft services on their own servers, rather than in the cloud, were somewhat spared.
Also Read

Global Microsoft outage disrupts India's corporate workday rhythm

Microsoft disruption exposes risks of relying on single provider: Experts

Microsoft service disruption impacts IndiGo's email support services

Microsoft 365 outage continues as company sees limited recovery in services

Microsoft outage disrupts Outlook, Teams for hours, hits users globally

ANOTHER OUTAGE FOR MICROSOFT The outage, reports of which started climbing around 1725 GMT on Thursday according to Ookla, is one of the longest in Microsoft's history and the second disruption to its services this year.
Microsoft said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online - its cloud-based email and scheduling hub - leaving unconnected applications operational.

The incident deepens questions about the global reliance on a handful of Big Tech companies that supply both the essential software and the cloud infrastructure that underpins it.
It also highlighted the dependence on Microsoft's workplace software, with outage reports spiking as employees began their workdays across Asia and Europe, according to Downdetector's parent company, Ookla.
Downdetector logged more than 7.4 million reports worldwide, peaking at nearly 20,000 a minute, more than 1,500 times normal levels.
"It shows how much of the working day now runs through one provider's email and collaboration tools," said Luke Kehoe, lead industry analyst at Ookla.
Microsoft shares closed flat at $523.88 on Friday. The stock has gained roughly 8% so far this year.

Disruptions and financial losses from the outage could result in numerous insurance claims, but the overall hit to insurers is expected to be limited, said Mario De Cicco, vice president of European financial institutions at Morningstar DBRS.
De Cicco estimated global insured losses from the incident at between $300 million and $500 million, well below the $400 million to $1.5 billion financial toll from the 2024 CrowdStrike outage that crashed more than 8 million Windows-based computers and caused widespread disruptions.
Microsoft also faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and in October last year. Last month, it reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software and a range of industries worldwide.

"The bigger worry is that this is not the first Microsoft 365 outage this year," said Josh Gilbert, a market analyst at trading platform eToro.
"If reliability starts to look like a recurring problem, it hands every IT department a reason to think twice before putting even more of their business in one provider's hands."
Still, some analysts have questioned whether such incidents can push customers on to rivals due to the steep switching costs of replacing tools embedded so deeply in daily operations.
TRADES HAD TO BE CONFIRMED BY FAX A spokesperson for the UK government said it was working with Microsoft to find a solution for the outage that hit organizations such as the NHS and London's Metropolitan Police.

Lack of access to emails and other services was impacting the Metropolitan Police's ability to report some crimes online, though its ability to respond to calls was not affected.
The NHS said its local services were turning to alternate measures such as using IT systems or paper records.
For businesses, the fallout was widespread.
European exchange operator Euronext reported email disruptions, British insurer Aviva activated backups for its earnings calls and Danish shipping giant Maersk warned customers of delayed updates.
American AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic also faced issues with Microsoft connectors, while Indian airlines IndiGo, Akasa Air and Air India said their email support services were impacted.

The outage also disrupted fund management at Taiwanese securities firms, life insurers, and investment trust companies. One of the companies went as far as cancelling a bond repurchase transaction, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters.
Another Taiwanese financial company resorted to using fax to confirm trades, a second source said.
In the US, electric truck maker Workhorse Group rescheduled its results on Thursday to November 16, while Switzerland's Richemont briefly delayed its first-half results announcement on Friday.
In Australia, where the spy agency and federal police were among organizations caught in the outage, Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft does not suspect a cyberattack.

"The impact that they are dealing with ... is very much on email systems," the minister added. 

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１３日 ロイター] - 米ダラス地区連銀のローガン総裁は１３日、同連銀が主催する会議で、米国債市場は金利の変動局面がありながらも「極めて良好に」機能しており、銀行もこの３年間で緊急時の資金調達手段へのアクセスを改善させていると述べた。また、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）はこの両面で支援手段を強化する措置を講じるべきだとした。

ローガン氏はニューヨーク連銀で公開市場操作の責任者を務めた経歴を持ち、ＦＲＢの実務的な政策手段に関して影響力がある人物だ。

米国債市場の機能を下支えするＦＲＢの取り組みについて「金融政策と相反する目的で作用することは避けなければならない」ことが極めて重要だと指摘。「とりわけ、より引き締め的な政策が必要と見られる経済環境においては、不必要な景気刺激を与えることなく市場機能を支える手段を強化することが、連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）にとって賢明だと考える」と述べた。

ローガン氏は現時点で市場介入が必要だとは考えていないことを明確にした。ただ、現在進行中のような政策引き締め局面での介入は、ＦＲＢの対外発信を難しくすると警告。「歴史的に見て、市場機能を支えるためのＦＲＢの介入は、ＦＯＭＣが同時に経済活動を刺激したいと考えていた時期に行われてきた。同じ資産購入が、金融緩和の提供と市場流動性の下支えという二つの目的を果たすことができた」とした上で、「仮に今、米国債市場の機能不全が生じたとしても、ＦＯＭＣは同じ資産購入で二つの目標を達成するという恵まれた状況にはない。たとえＦＯＭＣが緩和を望んだとしても、一つの手段で二つの目標を達成しようとすれば、情報発信が不明瞭になり、断固とした行動を取ることがより難しくなる」と述べた。

ローガン氏は、インフレが高すぎる水準で推移しているため、政策をより引き締め的にする必要があるとの持論を改めて示した。１０日には、少なくともあと２回、おそらく速やかに０．２５％ずつ利上げを行うべきだとの主張を展開していた。

items.title: エヌビディア、トップ後任にアームＣＥＯ浮上　フアン氏復帰求める声も＝報道
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１３日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手エヌビディアの取締役会が、辞任したジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）の後任探しの一環で、英半導体設計大手アームのレネ・ハースＣＥＯに接触したことが分かった。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）が１３日、関係筋の話として報じた。一方、一部従業員がフアン氏の復帰を求めているとの報道も出ている。

ＦＴによると、ハース氏は後任候補の一人に挙がっているが、正式な就任要請が出されるか、またその場合、ハース氏が応じるかは定かではない。

ハース氏はエヌビディアに７年勤務し、コンピューティング製品事業のバイスプレジデント兼ゼネラルマネジャーに昇進した後、２０１３年にアームに入社。２２年にアームのＣＥＯに就任し、２３年の米ナスダック市場への上場を主導した。

エヌビディアの取締役会は、後任ＣＥＯ探しを委託する人材紹介会社を選定している段階で、候補者には誰にも正式に接触していないと説明。声明で「社内外を問わず、個々の候補者について臆測するのは時期尚早だ」と表明した。

米テクノロジー誌ワイアードが１２日夜に報じたところによると、フアン氏の辞任前、エヌビディアの古参エンジニアが社内への投稿で、何らかの措置を講じる前に従業員の思いを考慮するよう取締役会に求めていた。

ワイアードが確認した社内のやりとりによると、この投稿にはその後１６００件を超えるコメントが寄せられ、フアン氏を復帰させる方法を探るよう取締役会に求める声が複数あった。

これとは別に、富豪のイーロン・マスク氏はＸへの投稿で、フアン氏の復帰を求める署名活動が進められており、自らも署名すると表明した。マスク氏がワイアードの報じた社内の動きを指しているかどうかは不明。

エヌビディアはワイアードの報道とマスク氏の投稿についてコメントを控えた。アームもコメントを控えた。ロイターはこれらの報道を独自に確認できていない。

米上場アーム株は約５％安で取引を終えた。エヌビディア株の終値は約２％安となり、時価総額は１週間で約５７３０億ドル減少した。

エヌビディアのフアン氏を巡っては、中国のスパイと疑われている女性や社内幹部との不倫疑惑が取り沙汰され、１２日に辞任が発表された。後任が正式に決まるまで、コレット・クレス最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）が暫定ＣＥＯを務める。

共同創業者のフアン氏は３０年以上にわたり、エヌビディアの技術開発戦略、中国向け輸出を巡る地政学的交渉、人工知能（ＡＩ）分野への投資などを主導する「実務型トップ」だった。

一部アナリストは、次期ＣＥＯの下では、こうしたフアン氏主導の経営体制が見直される可能性があるとみている。

後任候補としては、ハース氏のほか、クレス暫定ＣＥＯ、エヌビディアのハイパースケール・高性能コンピューティング担当バイスプレジデントであるイアン・バック氏、ＡＭＤのリサ・スーＣＥＯ、マイクロンのサンジェイ・メロトラＣＥＯらの名前が挙がっている。

また、トランプ米大統領は１２日、交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で、アップルのティム・クック前ＣＥＯが後任として適任との考えを示した。
